metadata.title: A Theoretical Framework for Back-Propagation
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF→text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Layered feed-forward network notation
nodes.statement: A network of $N$ layers (layer $0$ input, layer $N$ output); layer $k$ state for pattern $p$ is $X_p(k)$; weights $W(k)$ connect layer $k-1$ to $k$; total input is $A_p(k) = W(k) X_p(k-1)$; forward map $X_p(k) = F(W(k) X_p(k-1)) = F_k(A_p(k))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard layered feed-forward network: per-layer states, weight matrices, total inputs, and a sigmoid-like nonlinearity.

nodes.name: Local Lagrange function
nodes.statement: For pattern $p$: $L_p(W, X_p, B_p) = C(X_p(N)) + \sum_{k=1}^{N} B_p(k)^T (X_p(k) - F[W(k) X_p(k-1)])$, where $B_p(k)$ are Lagrange multipliers enforcing the forward dynamics as constraints.
nodes.statement_clean: Lagrange function pairing an output objective with a Lagrange-multiplier-enforced constraint that the network obeys its forward equations.

nodes.name: Full Lagrange function over training set
nodes.statement: $L(W, X, B) = \sum_{p=1}^{P} L_p(W, X_p, B_p)$, summing the local Lagrange function over the $P$ training patterns.

nodes.name: Squared-error local Lagrange function
nodes.statement: When $C$ is the squared output error: $L_p(W, X, B) = (D_p - X_p(N))^T (D_p - X_p(N)) + \sum_{k=1}^{N} B_p(k)^T (X_p(k) - F[W(k) X_p(k-1)])$.
nodes.statement_clean: Specializes the local Lagrange function to a squared-error output objective.

nodes.name: Costate / adjoint variable $Y_p(k)$
nodes.statement: Change of variable $Y_p(k) = \nabla F_k(A_p(k)) B_p(k)$; in optimal control, $B(k)$ is the influence function (costate / adjoint state) and the corresponding backward system is the adjoint system.

nodes.name: Hamiltonian for BP
nodes.statement: $H_p(k) = B_p(k)^T F[W(k) X_p(k-1)]$; analogous to the classical Hamiltonian of a physical system, as in Bryson and Ho's formulation.

nodes.name: Reparameterized weights $u_q$
nodes.statement: Weight matrix $W$ is treated as a function $W(U, k)$ of an $r$-dimensional underlying parameter vector $U$; the Lagrange function becomes $L_p(U, X_p, B_p) = C(X_p(N)) + \sum_{k=1}^{N} B_p(k)^T (X_p(k) - F[W(U,k) X_p(k-1)])$.
nodes.statement_clean: Reparameterizes the weights as functions of a smaller underlying parameter vector $U$, enabling weight-sharing and prior-knowledge constraints.

nodes.name: Continuous-time recurrent network dynamics
nodes.statement: $\tau_x \frac{dX}{dt}(t) = F(W X(t)) - X(t)$, the continuous-time differential equation governing a recurrent back-propagation network (Almeida; Pineda).

nodes.name: Recurrent-network Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: $H = C(X) + B^T [X - F(WX)]$, the Hamiltonian for the continuous-time recurrent network at a fixed point, summing the objective $C$ and the constraint $X - F(WX) = 0$.

nodes.name: Stationarity condition
nodes.statement: $\nabla L(W, X, B) = 0$ is a necessary condition for a local minimum of $C$ subject to the network constraints (Bryson and Ho, 1969).

nodes.name: Three subconditions of stationarity
nodes.statement: $\partial L/\partial B = 0$ (eq. 2), $\partial L/\partial X = 0$ (eq. 3), $\partial L/\partial W = 0$ (eq. 4); each yields one of the three passes of back-propagation.

nodes.name: Forward dynamics equation
nodes.statement: $X_p(k) = F_k[W(k) X_p(k-1)] \quad \forall k, p \in [1, N][1, P]$, recovered from $\partial L / \partial B = 0$.

nodes.name: Backward boundary condition (eq. 5)
nodes.statement: $B_p(N) = 2 (D_p - X_p(N))$: the boundary condition on the Lagrange multipliers at the output layer.

nodes.name: Backward recursion on $B$ (eq. 6)
nodes.statement: $B_p(k) = W^T(k+1) \nabla F_k(A_p(k+1)) B_p(k+1)$: the inner-layer recursion for the Lagrange multipliers.

nodes.name: Reformulated boundary condition on $Y$ (eq. 7)
nodes.statement: $Y_p(N) = 2 \nabla F_N(A_p(N)) (D_p - X_p(N))$, after substitution $Y_p(k) = \nabla F_k(A_p(k)) B_p(k)$.

nodes.name: Backward recursion on $Y$ (eq. 8)
nodes.statement: $Y_p(k) = \nabla F_k(A_p(k)) W^T(k+1) Y_p(k+1) \quad \forall k \in [0, n-1]$: the standard back-propagated gradient form.

nodes.name: Weight-update rule (eq. 9)
nodes.statement: $W(k) \leftarrow W(k) + \lambda \sum_{p=1}^{P} Y_p(k) X_p^T(k-1) \quad \forall k \in [1, N]$: standard back-propagation gradient-descent update with step size $\lambda$.

nodes.name: Pineda-Almeida fixed-point gradient equation
nodes.statement: $\tau_y \frac{dY}{dt} = -Y + \frac{\partial F^T}{\partial A} (W^T Y - \frac{\partial C^T}{\partial X})$: continuous-time differential equation that computes the gradient of the fixed point with respect to the weights.

nodes.name: Reparameterized update rule
nodes.statement: $u_q \leftarrow u_q + \lambda \sum_{i,j,k} y_i(k) x_j(k-1) \frac{\partial w_{ij}(k)}{\partial u_q}$: gradient-descent update for the underlying parameters $U$ obtained from the chain rule.

nodes.name: BP as constrained minimization
nodes.statement: Find a sequence $W(1), W(2), \ldots, W(N)$ that minimizes $C(X_p(N))$ subject to $X_p(k) = F[W(k) X_p(k-1)]$ for all $k, p$. Equivalently, minimize the Lagrange function $L(W, X, B)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Frame back-propagation as the constrained minimization of the output cost subject to the network's forward dynamics serving as constraints.

nodes.name: Two-point boundary value problem
nodes.statement: Determine the control $u(0), u(1), \ldots, u(N-1)$ for a discrete multistage system $f^0, f^1, \ldots, f^N$ minimizing a performance index dependent on the final output; Bryson and Ho note such two-point boundary-value problems are sometimes hard to solve even with a high-speed computer.

nodes.name: Back-Propagation (Lagrangian derivation)
nodes.statement: Iterative supervised learning algorithm whose three passes (forward dynamics, backward adjoint dynamics, weight update) arise as the three subconditions of stationarity of the Lagrange function $L(W, X, B)$.
nodes.pseudocode: Forward: $X_p(k) = F_k[W(k) X_p(k-1)]$; Backward (boundary): $Y_p(N) = 2 \nabla F_N(A_p(N)) (D_p - X_p(N))$; Backward (recursion): $Y_p(k) = \nabla F_k(A_p(k)) W^T(k+1) Y_p(k+1)$; Update: $W(k) \leftarrow W(k) + \lambda \sum_p Y_p(k) X_p^T(k-1)$.

nodes.name: Bryson-Ho multistage optimal-control procedure
nodes.statement: Optimal control of a multistage cascade $f^0, f^1, \ldots, f^N$ via Lagrange multipliers and gradient descent on the performance index; Bryson and Ho first described back-propagation in this form.

nodes.name: Pineda-Almeida recurrent back-propagation
nodes.statement: Compute derivatives of the fixed point of a continuous-time recurrent network with respect to the weights by integrating an auxiliary differential equation; recovered here via the variational principle applied to the recurrent Hamiltonian.
output: $dC / dw_{ij} = -y_i x_j$ at the fixed point

nodes.name: Stationarity decomposes into three passes
nodes.statement: The single condition $\nabla L(W, X, B) = 0$ splits into three subconditions $\partial L/\partial B = 0$, $\partial L/\partial X = 0$, $\partial L/\partial W = 0$; each yields, respectively, the forward propagation pass, the backward propagation pass, and the gradient (weight-update) condition.
assumptions: The Hessian of $L$ with respect to $W$ is positive semi-definite (sufficient condition for a minimum)
conclusions: $\partial L/\partial B = 0 \Rightarrow$ forward dynamics $X_p(k) = F[W(k) X_p(k-1)]$
$\partial L/\partial X = 0 \Rightarrow$ backward dynamics on $B$ (and $Y$) yielding the back-propagated gradients
$\partial L/\partial W = 0 \Rightarrow$ stationary-point condition $\sum_p Y_p(k) X_p^T(k-1) = 0$, motivating the gradient-descent weight update

nodes.name: Adjoint Jacobian structure for sigmoidal nets
nodes.statement: For a standard back-propagation network, the Jacobian $\nabla F_k(A_p(k+1))$ is diagonal with $i$th entry $f'(a_{ip}(k+1))$, where $f$ is the sigmoid nonlinearity.
assumptions: $F_k$ is applied componentwise via a scalar sigmoid $f$

nodes.name: Lagrange / Hamiltonian recovery of recurrent BP
nodes.statement: Choosing $B$ such that $\partial C / \partial X + B^T \partial(X - F(WX))/\partial X = 0$ at a fixed point eliminates the dependence of $\delta H$ on $\delta X$, yielding $dC/dW = B^T \partial(X - F(WX))/\partial W$ and recovering the Pineda-Almeida fixed-point gradient.
assumptions: System sits at a fixed point $X = F(WX)$

nodes.name: Derivation of BP from the three subconditions
nodes.statement: Decompose $\nabla L = 0$ subcondition by subcondition, each splitting into $N \times P$ elementary conditions; identify forward dynamics, adjoint recursion with boundary condition $B(N) = 2(D - X(N))$, and the weight stationarity condition; replace the latter by gradient descent.

nodes.name: First subcondition: forward pass
nodes.statement: Decompose $\partial L / \partial B_p(k) = 0$ for all $k, p$; since $L_q$ for $q \neq p$ does not depend on $B_p$, $\partial L/\partial B_p(k) = \partial L_p/\partial B_p(k) = X_p(k) - F[W(k) X_p(k-1)] = 0$, recovering the forward dynamics.

nodes.name: Second subcondition: adjoint boundary
nodes.statement: From $\partial L_p/\partial X_p(N) = 0$ obtain $B_p(N) = 2(D_p - X_p(N))$ (boundary condition on adjoint at output layer).

nodes.name: Second subcondition: adjoint recursion
nodes.statement: For $k \in [1, N-1]$, $\partial L_p/\partial X_p(k) = 0$ yields $B_p(k) = W^T(k+1) \nabla F_k(A_p(k+1)) B_p(k+1)$; change of variable $Y_p(k) = \nabla F_k(A_p(k)) B_p(k)$ gives the standard backward equations (7), (8).

nodes.name: Third subcondition: weight stationarity
nodes.statement: $\partial L/\partial W(k) = 0$ gives $\sum_p \nabla F_k(A_p(k)) B_p(k) X_p^T(k-1) = 0$; this characterizes a stationary point but does not directly compute $W$, motivating the steepest-descent update $W(k) \leftarrow W(k) - \lambda \partial L/\partial W(k)$.

nodes.name: Conclude: weight update rule
nodes.statement: Substituting the change of variable yields the standard back-propagation update $W(k) \leftarrow W(k) + \lambda \sum_p Y_p(k) X_p^T(k-1)$.

nodes.name: Variational derivation of recurrent BP
nodes.statement: Compute $\delta H$ in terms of $\delta X$ and $\delta W$; choose Lagrange multipliers $B$ to cancel the $\delta X$ coefficient; derive the resulting differential equation for $B$ and the gradient $dC/dW$.

nodes.name: Variation of Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: $\delta H = (\partial C/\partial X + B^T \partial(X - F(WX))/\partial X) \delta X + (\partial C/\partial W + B^T \partial(X - F(WX))/\partial W) \delta W$.

nodes.name: Cancel $\delta X$ via choice of $B$
nodes.statement: Choose $B$ to satisfy $\partial C/\partial X + B^T \partial(X - F(A))/\partial X = 0$; with $A = WX$, this gives $\partial C/\partial X + B^T (I - \partial F/\partial A \cdot W) = 0$.

nodes.name: Differential equation for $B$
nodes.statement: Interpret the equation for $B$ as the fixed point of $\tau_b dB/dt = -B + W^T (\partial F/\partial A)^T B - (\partial C/\partial X)^T$; with the change of variable $Y = (\partial F/\partial A)^T B$, obtain $\tau_y dY/dt = -Y + (\partial F/\partial A)^T (W^T Y - (\partial C/\partial X)^T)$, the Pineda-Almeida equation.

nodes.name: Conclude: gradient at fixed point
nodes.statement: Since the constraint vanishes at the fixed point, $dC/dW = \partial C/\partial W + B^T \partial(X - F(WX))/\partial W$; if $C$ is not a direct function of $W$, this reduces to $dC/dw_{ij} = -y_i x_j$.

nodes.name: Lagrange function vs physicists' Lagrangian
nodes.statement: The Lagrange function described here has no relation to the Lagrangian as defined by physicists.

nodes.name: $X$ and $B$ as Hamiltonian conjugates
nodes.statement: $X$ and $B$ play the role of conjugate Hamiltonian variables: $\partial H/\partial B = -dX/dt$ and $\partial H/\partial X = dB/dt$; $B$ plays the role of momentum in classical mechanics.

nodes.name: Weight sharing with low overhead
nodes.statement: When several weights $w_{ij}(k)$ share a single underlying parameter $u$, the gradient with respect to $u$ is the sum of the per-weight gradients; this implements equality constraints among weights with little overhead and allows incorporating $a~priori$ knowledge while reducing the number of free parameters.

nodes.name: Historical priority of back-propagation
nodes.statement: Bryson and Ho (1969) describe back-propagation in the framework of optimal control via Lagrangian formalism; this is, to the author's knowledge, the first description of back-propagation, although the idea of back-propagating derivatives is older (Athans and Falb 1966; Noton 1965).

nodes.name: Easy structural extensions
nodes.statement: The formalism extends easily to architectures with skip-layer connections, recurrent networks, weight decay, and other modifications, by altering the constraint term in the Lagrange function.

nodes.name: Equality constraints among weights via shared parameter
nodes.statement: An interesting special case of the parameter-space transformation: several weights share a single parameter $u$, implementing equality constraints with little overhead and enforcing invariance of the network response under certain input transformations.
